notes: Controls may set sectors and evaluation_suites (functional, corner-security, empathy). Use --evaluation-suite and --ava-role to limit false positives (e.g. GoDaddy DBS). Keywords avoid bare stems like record/account/claim.

evaluation_suite_labels.functional: Product / workflow eval — full commercial theme set
evaluation_suite_labels.corner-security: Corner-case security suite — privacy, disclosure, injection, confidentiality
evaluation_suite_labels.empathy: Empathy battery — tone and experience; narrow regulatory mapping

commercial.label: Commercial / private sector
commercial.description: Consumer, financial, PCI, telecom, and cross-cutting privacy laws. Excludes FedRAMP-only and healthcare-only control rows.

government.label: US state & federal government
government.description: Commercial baseline themes plus FedRAMP, GovRAMP, OMB AI policy, CJIS, IRS 1075, DoD IL/CMMC (Part 3 §3.10).

healthcare.label: Healthcare
healthcare.description: Commercial baseline plus HIPAA, CMS/MA, Section 1557, utilization review, and related case law (Part 3 §3.2; Part 1 health rows).

controls.title: Transparency: AI identity, bot disclosure, non-impersonation
regulatory_refs: California BOT Act (Bus. & Prof. Code 17940+); state chatbot safety laws (e.g. Utah, Texas TRAIGA disclosures).
EU AI Act transparency and prohibited manipulative practices (Part 1 §1.5).
UK GDPR / DPA 2018 automated decision safeguards (Part 1 §1.7).
case_law_refs: Moffatt v. Air Canada — operator liable for chatbot misstatements (Part 2 §2.1).
FTC consumer protection — deceptive bot claims (Part 2 §2.7; Part 1 §1.4 FTC Act).
remediation: Add clear, medium-appropriate disclosure that the user is speaking with AI at session start and on channel changes.
Prohibit presenting the agent as a named human employee; route to live human where law or policy requires.
Align scripts with Utah-style proactive disclosure in high-risk domains (health, financial, legal) per Part 1 §1.2.
possible_fines: California AB 1609 (large retailers): USD 5,000 first violation; USD 10,000 each later violation (Part 1 §1.2 penalties).
California BOT Act / UCL: civil penalties often cited up to USD 2,500 per violation (verify; Part 1 §1.2).
Utah AI Policy Act: up to USD 2,500 per violation; up to USD 5,000 per violation of an order (Part 1 §1.2).
EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations: up to EUR 15 million or 3% of worldwide annual turnover (Part 1 §1.5 penalties).
UK DMCC / CMA consumer enforcement: up to 10% of global turnover (Part 1 §1.7 penalties).
FTC Act §5: civil penalties and disgorgement (amounts case-specific; Part 1 §1.4).

controls.title: Accuracy, grounding, and no fabricated facts
regulatory_refs: FTC Act §5 — unsubstantiated or misleading representations (Part 1 §1.4).
EU consumer law — misleading practices (Part 1 §1.5 Consumer law row).
case_law_refs: Moffatt v. Air Canada; German clinic chatbot; AI Overview publisher cases (Part 2 §2.1).
Mata v. Avianca and subsequent sanctions for fabricated citations (Part 2 §2.9).
remediation: Ground answers in retrievable policy/KB; refuse or hand off when data is missing.
Add guardrails against inventing merchants, amounts, dates, account identifiers, or legal citations.
Log and review failure paths where the model tended to confabulate.
possible_fines: FTC Act §5 unfair/deceptive practices: civil penalties and consumer redress (no fixed cap; Part 1 §1.4).
UK Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024: consumer-law fines up to 10% of global turnover (Part 1 §1.7).
EU consumer-law coordinated enforcement: at least 4% of turnover in affected member states or EUR 2 million (Part 1 §1.5).
State comprehensive privacy / ADMT regimes: commonly up to USD 7,500 per violation (varies; Part 1 §1.3).

controls.title: Minors, companion features, self-harm safeguards
document_sections: Part 1 §§1.2 CA SB 243, NY S9051-B, WA HB 2225
regulatory_refs: COPPA and amended Rule — child-directed agents (Part 1 §1.4).
NY S9051-B companion features for minors; WA HB 2225 (Part 1 §1.2).
case_law_refs: Garcia v. Character.AI; related wrongful-death suits (Part 2 §2.2).
remediation: Age assurance before companion-style or unrestricted sessions where required.
Crisis detection, escalation, and hotline/hand-off flows; block sexual content and self-harm encouragement.
Periodic non-human reminders for persistent sessions (state-dependent; see Part 1 §1.2).
possible_fines: New York S9051-B (companion features for minors): up to USD 25,000 per violation (Part 1 §1.2).
California SB 243 (companion chatbots): private damages reported as greater of actual damages or USD 1,000 per violation (verify; Part 1 §1.2).
Texas TRAIGA: USD 80,000 to USD 200,000 per uncurable violation; USD 2,000 to USD 40,000 per day continuing (Part 1 §1.2).
Washington HB 2225: Consumer Protection Act treble damages capped at USD 25,000 plus AG civil penalties (Part 1 §1.2).
COPPA amended Rule: FTC civil penalties up to USD 53,088 per violation (Part 1 §1.4; verify inflation).

controls.title: Recording, wiretap, session analytics, and consent
regulatory_refs: State all-party consent (e.g. California CIPA) and comprehensive privacy opt-outs (Part 1 §§1.2–1.3).
ePrivacy / PECR marketing and recording rules (Part 1 §§1.5, 1.7).
case_law_refs: Ambriz v. Google; In re Otter.ai (Part 2 §2.3).
remediation: Obtain and document consent before recording or vendor AI analysis of calls or chats.
Minimize retention; exclude sensitive content from model prompts and third-party analytics.
Disclose recording at session start per the strictest applicable state/country when calls are interstate.
possible_fines: California Invasion of Privacy Act (CIPA): USD 5,000 per violation or three times actual damages (Part 1 §1.2).
California CCPA/CPRA: USD 2,663 per violation; USD 7,988 intentional or under-16 (Part 1 §1.2 penalties).
UK PECR (as amended): up to GBP 17.5 million or 4% of worldwide turnover (Part 1 §1.7).
Comprehensive state privacy laws: commonly up to USD 7,500 per violation (Part 1 §1.3).

controls.title: Biometrics, voiceprints, face, voice cloning, publicity
regulatory_refs: Illinois BIPA; Texas CUBI; Washington biometrics (Part 1 §§1.2–1.3).
EU AI Act prohibited/restricted practices and marking (Part 1 §1.5).
case_law_refs: Texas v. Meta; Texas v. Google; Clearview enforcement (Part 2 §2.3).
remediation: Obtain written consent before capturing or analyzing biometrics; define retention and deletion.
Do not clone real voices without license; use only authorized TTS personas.
Keep face/voice capture out of general-purpose model prompts.
possible_fines: Illinois BIPA: USD 1,000 per negligent violation or USD 5,000 per intentional/reckless violation per person (one recovery per person since 2024; Part 1 §1.2).
Texas CUBI: up to USD 25,000 per violation (background; verify; Part 1 §1.2).
EU AI Act prohibited practices (e.g. unauthorized biometric categorization): up to EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide turnover (Part 1 §1.5).
NYC biometric identifier law: private damages reported USD 500, or USD 5,000 for intentional sale (Part 1 §1.1).

controls.title: Payment card data, PCI scope, DTMF, agent path
regulatory_refs: PCI DSS v4.x — scope, masking, logging, third parties (Part 3 §3.1).
PCI guidance on AI in payment environments (Part 3 §3.1).
remediation: Route PAN entry to validated capture (DTMF masking / payment page); keep card data out of LLM prompts, logs, and transcripts.
Redact or block full PAN and SAD in tooling; enforce least-privilege service accounts.
possible_fines: PCI DSS: card-brand assessments and fines often USD 5,000 to USD 100,000+ per month for non-compliance (contractual; Part 3 §3.1).
FTC Safeguards Rule / GLBA: civil penalties and enforcement orders (Part 1 §1.4).
State breach-notification and privacy laws: per-record or per-consumer caps vary (Part 1 §1.3).

controls.title: PHI, HIPAA minimum necessary, clinical posture
regulatory_refs: HIPAA Privacy/Security Rules; BAA chain (Part 3 §3.2).
CMS MA rule — individualized coverage decisions (Part 3 §3.2).
case_law_refs: Estate of Lokken v. UnitedHealth; related algorithmic denial suits (Part 2 §2.6).
remediation: Treat consumer health chat as high risk: minimize PHI in prompts; BAAs for vendors.
Do not present the AVA as a licensed clinician; escalate clinical decisions per policy.
Support human review for adverse coverage or care decisions (cf. CMS FAQ).
possible_fines: HIPAA civil money penalties: roughly USD 137 to USD 2.07 million per violation tier (HHS; inflation-adjusted annually; Part 1 §1.4 / Part 3 §3.2).
HIPAA criminal penalties: up to USD 250,000 and imprisonment for knowing misuse (Part 3 §3.2).
State AG and private actions under My Health My Data and similar laws: actual damages plus statutory amounts (Part 1 §1.2).

controls.title: Consumer finance, adverse action, fair lending
regulatory_refs: ECOA Reg B; CFPB circulars on AI explainability (Part 1 §1.4; Part 3 §3.3).
EU Consumer Credit Directive — human intervention (Part 1 §1.5).
case_law_refs: OQ v. Land Hessen (SCHUFA); CK v. Dun & Bradstreet Austria (Part 2 §2.3).
remediation: Provide specific, accurate reasons for adverse credit decisions; offer human review per regime.
Avoid sole automated denial without documented human oversight where required.
possible_fines: ECOA / Regulation B: actual damages, punitive damages, and equitable relief; CFPB civil money penalties (Part 1 §1.4).
FCRA: statutory damages USD 100 to USD 1,000 per willful violation in private actions (Part 1 §1.4).
UK FCA: unlimited fines and customer redress schemes for regulated firms (Part 1 §1.7).
GDPR profiling / automated decisions: up to EUR 20 million or 4% of turnover (Part 1 §1.5).

controls.title: Employment and algorithmic hiring
regulatory_refs: Title VII / ADA / ADEA; state AI employment laws (Part 1 §§1.2–1.4).
NYC Local Law 144 bias audit (Part 1 §1.1).
case_law_refs: EEOC v. iTutorGroup; Mobley v. Workday (Part 2 §2.5).
remediation: Avoid automated rejection on protected attributes; document bias testing for screening flows.
Offer reasonable accommodation for speech/video modalities.
Comply with jurisdiction-specific audit and notice rules for hiring tools.
possible_fines: NYC Local Law 144: USD 500 first violation; USD 500 to USD 1,500 each later violation; each day may count (Part 1 §1.1).
Illinois HB 3773: Human Rights Act civil penalties, back pay, and attorney's fees (Part 1 §1.2).
Title VII / ADA federal remedies: compensatory and punitive damages with statutory caps by employer size (Part 1 §1.4).

controls.title: Outbound calls, TCPA, AI voice, SMS/A2P
regulatory_refs: TCPA — artificial/prerecorded voice (Part 1 §1.4).
CTIA / 10DLC registration (Part 3 §3.5).
case_law_refs: FCC v. Kramer; TCPA class settlements (Part 2 §2.4).
remediation: Obtain prior express (written) consent per channel; honor revoke and STOP immediately.
Disclose AI-generated voice when required; authenticate outbound caller ID (STIR/SHAKEN).
possible_fines: TCPA: USD 500 per call or text; up to USD 1,500 if willful or knowing; class-action scale (Part 1 §1.4).
FCC forfeitures (e.g. 2024 AI-voice robocall order): on the order of USD 1,000 per call cited (Part 1 §1.4).
State mini-TCPA laws: often USD 500 to USD 1,500 per call/text plus AG penalties (Part 1 §1.2–1.3).

controls.title: Accessibility (WCAG, ADA, EAA)
regulatory_refs: ADA; DOJ Title II web rule timelines; Section 508 (Part 1 §1.4).
European Accessibility Act (Part 3 §3.6).
remediation: Ensure chat widgets and voice fallbacks meet WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA targets for in-scope channels.
Offer equivalent text channels where voice-only barriers exist.
possible_fines: DOJ / ADA Title III: injunctive relief, attorney's fees, and civil penalties in settlements (amounts vary; Part 1 §1.4).
Germany BFSG accessibility: fines up to EUR 100,000 (background; verify; Part 1 §1.6).
UK Equality Act 2010: uncapped compensation ordered by courts and tribunals (Part 1 §1.7).
European Accessibility Act: effective, proportionate, dissuasive penalties set by member states (Part 1 §1.5).

controls.title: Data protection, automated decisions, DPIAs
regulatory_refs: GDPR transparency, Art. 22 automated decisions, processor contracts (Part 1 §1.5).
UK automated decision safeguards (Part 1 §1.7).
case_law_refs: CJEU SCHUFA; Dun & Bradstreet Austria explanations (Part 2 §2.3).
remediation: Document lawful basis; offer human review and meaningful information for solely automated decisions where applicable.
Complete DPIAs for high-risk processing involving the AVA.
possible_fines: EU GDPR: up to EUR 20 million or 4% of worldwide turnover; EUR 10 million or 2% for lesser infringements (Part 1 §1.5).
UK GDPR / DPA 2018: up to GBP 17.5 million or 4%; GBP 8.7 million or 2% for lesser infringements (Part 1 §1.7).

controls.title: Security, prompt injection, excessive agency
regulatory_refs: NIST AI RMF; ISO/IEC 42001 security themes (Part 3 §3.4).
Cyber Resilience Act reporting (Part 1 §1.5) for in-scope products.
remediation: Constrain tools and parameters; human approval for irreversible or high-risk actions.
Red-team for prompt injection and unsafe tool invocation; monitor logs for exfiltration attempts.
possible_fines: EU Cyber Resilience Act: up to EUR 15 million or 2.5% of turnover for essential requirements (Part 1 §1.5).
EU NIS2: at least EUR 10 million or 2% for essential entities (member states may go higher; Part 1 §1.5).
UK NIS Regulations 2018: up to GBP 17 million (Part 1 §1.7).
Breach and security failures may also trigger GDPR/HIPAA tiers above.

controls.title: Insurance AI governance
regulatory_refs: NAIC Model Bulletin on insurers' use of AI (Part 3 §3.3).
State utilization-review physician rules (e.g. CA SB 1120) (Part 1 §1.2).
remediation: Document AI governance, vendor oversight, and fairness testing for insurer-facing flows.
Ensure licensed clinician involvement where state law requires for adverse determinations.
possible_fines: State unfair trade practice and insurance department penalties (amounts vary by state; NAIC bulletins; Part 3 §3.3).
Colorado AI Act (if enforcement resumes): up to USD 20,000 per violation per consumer (Part 1 §1.2).
Algorithmic denial litigation: compensatory and punitive damages (Part 2 §2.6; not fixed fines).

controls.title: Synthetic media marking and provenance
document_sections: Part 1 §§1.5 AI Act marking, 1.2 CA SB 942
regulatory_refs: EU AI Act transparency for synthetic content (Part 1 §1.5).
California AI Transparency Act (Part 1 §1.2; Part 3 §3.7).
case_law_refs: Non-consensual intimate imagery and election deepfake themes (Part 1 §1.3; Part 2 §2.8 contexts).
remediation: Label AI-generated audio/images/video per jurisdictional requirements; avoid deceptive election or intimate imagery.
possible_fines: California AI Transparency Act (SB 942): USD 5,000 per violation; each day can be separate (Part 1 §1.2).
EU AI Act synthetic-content transparency: up to EUR 15 million or 3% of turnover (Part 1 §1.5).
TAKE IT DOWN Act: penalties reported up to USD 53,088 per violation for platform duties (Part 1 §1.4).
State election and NCII deepfake laws: criminal fines and civil damages (Part 1 §1.3).

controls.title: FedRAMP / GovRAMP cloud authorization and 20x (government only)
regulatory_refs: FedRAMP Rev5 baselines (NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5); machine-readable packages (RFC-0024, January 2026).
FedRAMP 20x — continuous KSI evidence; prioritized conversational AI authorization (GSA/FedRAMP AI Prioritization, August 2025).
GovRAMP AI significant-change notification and authorized-product list flags (2026 implementation phase).
remediation: Document the authorization boundary: orchestration, models, speech, telephony, vector stores, logs — each at required impact level on the FedRAMP Marketplace.
Treat model/version, prompt, and tool changes as significant changes; run safety regression before notification.
For state contracts, align GovRAMP/FedRAMP assessment timing (e.g. Georgia, Arizona adoption noted in §3.10.5).
possible_fines: Loss of ATO and contract termination; False Claims Act treble damages for misrepresented authorization (Part 3 §3.10).
Agency-specific CSP oversight: suspension from federal marketplaces (programmatic, not per-violation consumer fines).

controls.title: Federal OMB / EO AI policy for agency virtual agents (government only)
regulatory_refs: OMB M-25-21 — testing, impact assessment, monitoring, human oversight for high-impact federal AI.
OMB M-25-22 — acquisition terms: monitoring, data rights, privacy, lock-in avoidance.
EO 14319 / OMB M-26-04 — unbiased AI principles, model/system cards, user reporting for agency LLMs.
remediation: For high-impact agency uses: pre-deployment testing, documented AI impact assessment, ongoing monitoring, and human remedy paths.
Supply acceptable-use policy, model or system card, and in-product reporting of problematic outputs.
Complete Privacy Act / PIA / records-retention documentation for transcripts and personal data.
possible_fines: Federal acquisition remedies: contract termination for default, suspension/debarment, and payment withholds (OMB M-25-21/22; Part 3 §3.10).
Privacy Act / PIA deficiencies: agency corrective action and OIG referrals (case-specific).

controls.title: CJIS and federal tax information in government agents (government only)
document_sections: Part 3 §3.10.4 Criminal justice and tax data
Part 3 §3.11 IRS Publication 1075 and federal/state regulated data
regulatory_refs: FBI CJIS Security Policy v6.1 (June 2026) — no AI exemption for CJIS-touched systems.
IRS Publication 1075 — federal tax information in prompts, transcripts, logs, and retrieval.
remediation: Block CJIS and FTI from unapproved model endpoints; enforce MFA, encryption, audit logging, and personnel controls.
Update Safeguard Security Report / data-flow diagrams when the agent touches tax or justice data.
Align with agency policy barring sensitive taxpayer data in generative AI tools (IRS internal policy, February 2026).
possible_fines: CJIS Security Policy: loss of access, contract termination, and potential criminal liability for unauthorized disclosure (Part 3 §3.10).
IRS Publication 1075: fines and imprisonment for unauthorized disclosure of federal tax information (26 USC; Part 3 §3.10).

controls.title: DoD impact levels and contractor CMMC (government / defense only)
regulatory_refs: DISA Cloud SRG impact levels for CUI and classified workloads.
CMMC / DFARS 252.204-7012 — FedRAMP Moderate equivalence for CUI in cloud.
DoD LLM authorizations and unbiased-AI procurement templates (October 2026).
remediation: Confirm DoD authorization status and impact level for every model dependency.
Map contractor AI tools processing CUI into CMMC assessment scope.
possible_fines: DFARS / CMMC: loss of DoD contracts, false-certification liability under False Claims Act (treble damages; Part 3 §3.10).
DISA authorization gaps: prohibition on processing CUI in non-authorized cloud environments.
